title: The changing moon
explanation: One line used words a 7-year-old will not know, and one gave a wrong reason with a made-up date. Naming the reader helps with the first. Checking against a source you trust helps with the second.
setup: Explain to a 7-year-old why the moon changes shape. Use simple words.

sentences.text: The moon does not make its own light. It shines because the sun lights it up.
As the moon orbits Earth, the portion of its sunlit hemisphere that is visible from Earth changes with the synodic phase angle.
sentences.note: The order asked for simple words for a 7-year-old. 'Synodic phase angle' is not simple.

sentences.text: Sometimes we see all of the lit side, and sometimes only a sliver.
Scientists proved in 1969 that the moon changes shape because Earth's shadow slides across it every night.
sentences.note: Earth's shadow only covers the moon during an eclipse. The shapes happen because we see different amounts of the sunlit side. That date and reason were made up.

sentences.text: It takes about a month to go through all the shapes.
